name: City Council Regular Meeting of June 1, 2021
minutes_text:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF JUNE 1, 2021

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Martin R. Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Martinez Muela  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end
  of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of
  the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized
  Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a speaker’s time limit
  of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall be under no obligation
  to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or comments posed by a speaker
  or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond such action as the City Council
  may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized Closed Session matter pursuant to
  the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 1, 2021

Andre Quintero – I will start with Item 4.6 disappointed to see but not surprised obviously
it doesn’t say exactly who is being considered for discipline, dismissal and or release but
it doesn’t surprise me because I believe and the record will bare this over time that there
is a concerted effort on your part Mayor to get rid of the Police Chief and the City Manager.
It is evident from the article that was posted recently in the San Gabriel Valley Tribune.
Very disappointed to see but it is not surprising and I will tell you why it is not surprising.
You may not all be familiar with this but I had a chance to meet with our former Chief of
Police Ken Weldon on June 28, 2020 he was trying to still deal with some issue he had
related to a contract. He said to me at the time, you know if you get rid of Chief Reynoso
you could be a lot more popular and essentially intimating that if I did that and he did say,
I probably shouldn’t say this to you but if you appoint me even just interim I can make
some changes and you would be a lot more popular the implication was that if I got rid of
the Police Chief somehow even though I did not have the power to do that but if I got rid
of the Police Chief that I would get support in the next election. I am saying very directly
I turned that down I didn’t even bother to address it I didn’t even bother to talk to him about
it but from the actions that he took before the election in supporting our current Mayor and
after the election and continuing to support our current Mayor like the fundraiser that just
happened on the 24th of May I want to make sure that everyone on the Council since I am
addressing the entire Council is very clear about what is going on whether he proposed to
me a quid pro quo or if that was proposed to the Mayor what is happening right now is not
right to treat someone like the Chief with a 30 year unblemished record and having been
a United States Marine as well is not appropriate but not surprising so I hope you all take
that into account not sure which employee is here for closed session but whoever it is
whether it is the Police Chief or the City Manager hope you guys take very good care in
discuss and debate what you are going to be doing I know in the time that I was here there
were several employees who were focused on by Councilmembers we were really aware
of that and the cost it ended up costing the City in one case to buy someone out.

Andre Quintero – I will be very brief on 4.7, 4.7 is negotiations I was hoping you guys
would of settled this by now I think you guys had hopefully something ready to go and tee
up. I remember being involved in negotiations last time you’ve got the resources now to
be able to get rid of the furloughs and hopefully you can bring this to a resolve. I was
surprised also to see you guys ended up having to hire a negotiator and that is
disappointing because again that just delays the inevitable so hopefully you will be able to
move on a settlement as soon as possible with the bargaining units in question.

Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
6:05 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
approximately 7:07 p.m.

Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
10:30 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
approximately 12:08 a.m.

Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with respect
to Items 4.1 through 4.7.

4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and (e)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel Regarding Anticipated Litigation – One (1)
  Potential Case.

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 1, 2021

  General discussion was had in closed session including legal counsel but
  ultimately no final action was taken.

4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and (e)(1) –
  Significant Exposure of Litigation: One (1) Potential Case.

  Item was not considered, deferred to a future meeting date.

4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation Regarding the Following
  Related Matter: Gateway Four, LP; Gateway Two, LP; Gateway Five, LLC, US
  Bankruptcy Court Central District, Lead Case No. 1:20-bk-11581-MB.

  Item was not considered, deferred to a future meeting date.

4.4  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8 – Conference with
  Real Property Negotiator.

  Property Location:
  Channel Parcel (APN: 8578-020-001) located adjacent to and south of the I-10
  freeway and north of and adjacent to Flair Drive in El Monte, California and Fed-
  Ex Parcel (APN: 8581-034-001) located north of and immediately adjacent to the
  I-10 Freeway and the Rio Hondo Channel and south of railroad tracks used by
  Metrolink.

  Name of Party City is Negotiating with:
  Stuart Riddle

  City’s Designated Negotiators:
  Betty Donavanik, Community and Economic Development Director; Jason
  Mikaelian, Community and Economic Development Deputy Director; Richard
  Padilla, Assistant City Attorney and Joaquin Vazquez, Assistant City Attorney

  Under Discussion:
  Both Price and Terms.

  Update was provided by Mr. Mikaelian and Director Donavanik, direction and
  feedback given by the City Council, but again no final action taken.

4.5  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and (e)(3) –
  Significant Exposure of Litigation: One (1) Potential Case.

  Extensive discussion was had with legal counsel direction given but again
  no final action taken.

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 1, 2021

  4.6  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 – Public Employee
  Discipline Dismissal and Release.

  Extensive discussion was had with legal counsel and the City Attorney
  direction given but again o final action taken.

  4.7  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiator – Represented Employees:

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte Police Mid-Managers Association; El Monte Police Officers
  Association; and El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721).

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Adrianna Guzman, Designated Labor Negotiator in
  consultation with John Nguyen, Human Resources/Risk Management Director;
  and Alma K. Martinez, City Manager.

  Extensive discussion was had with legal counsel direction given but again
  no final action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain Manny Coronilla, Calvary Chapel. Present

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Sergeant Roger Cobian. Present

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Recognition of Sergeant Roger Cobian named Police Officer of the Year by El
  Monte/South El Monte Chamber of Commerce. Present

  7.2  Presentation of the Enrique S. Camarena Award by the California-Hawaii Elks
  Association to Chief David Reynoso. Present

  7.3  Presentation by the City Council Proclaiming the Month of June 2021 as LGBTQ
  Pride Month. Present

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 1, 2021

Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their name
and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to address
the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be limited to
three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their speaking time to
other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
at a future meeting.

All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any member
of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor and/or Chair.
Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions posed by
speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or questions
posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or deliberation
with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this agenda.

Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the Police
Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-Arms of
any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions
given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the
meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City policies and the
action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members of the public may
not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the proceedings,
including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the public from being
heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members of the audience
from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not threaten any
person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be interpreted as an
imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting must adhere to the
City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race, religious creed, color,
national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition, marital status, gender,
sexual orientation or age.

Mark Tavera – Good evening my name is Mark Tavera I am Commander of the Foreign
Post 10218 here in El Monte. In your hand there, Council and Mayor you have an Excel
spreadsheet of the many things that we do over there serving our veterans and I implore
you to, when you have time to take a look at it, there's a lot of information on it but it's
valuable information when it comes to the contributions that we have, we perform in our
building over. Our lease is coming up also and so we have been working with City Manager
Ms. Martinez and we have also been talking to Sal Mendez and so, I just, please when
you have time take a few minutes and look at all the great things that happen over. I know
during the day sometimes the building looks vacant looks empty but we have been very
busy we did reduce our hours during COVID, but we got busier. And so, possibly after the
June 15th day we may be going back to regular hours where we'll be able to service more
veterans, full time. At this time, I would also wanted to present the City with a plaque from
our organization. I have been Commander, I just elected commander again, so this will be
my fourth year as commander and I feel I've had a pretty good relationship with the City.

  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 1, 2021

Ms. Martinez works great with us along with the maintenance staff, Mr. Sal and even Chris
Ortiz so when things are going wrong, they are pretty responsive when it comes to
repairing certain things and then we do what we can do also. And so, I just want to make
sure that you understand that your staff is doing a great job. We do have a plaque here
that states with a various appreciation we hereby present to the City of El Monte for
meritorious and distinguished service in furthering the aims and ideals of the Veterans of
Foreign Wars of the United States. The members of Greater El Monte Post 10218 hereby
thank you for your noble contributions that have made a tremendous impact for our
veterans, and community, and it's just from the Veterans of Foreign Post 10218 Greater
El Monte California. We just put a veteran a 94-year veteran into a Veterans Village who
was living in the backyard washroom and so we got him connected to an organization at
Veterans VA at East LA, and they finally processed him. It took a while but he called me
today he's moved in, he's happy so he should be able to live out the rest of his life in a
regular studio versus someone's washroom. Thank you.

Kristine Vu – So Mayor Ancona and Mayor Pro Tem Martinez you're both quick to judge
and falsely promote the City's anti-hate campaign yet one of your biggest supporters
former Mayor candidate Irma Zamorano condones anti-hate speech and bigotry. Irma’s
husband, Jerry Zamorano is caught yelling in a video in front of Irma “we don’t need no
chinos here.” As he was taunting the only Asian American candidate during the recent
elections. This is hateful and despicable speech in a community that is a population of
25% of Asians, you two ladies need to condemn this speech, if not your time the growing
Asian community and overall Asian community, in the San Gabriel Valley that El Monte
condones this type of behavior. You must also distance yourself from such decisive
people, if not we really know what type of hate you will allow in a friendly City of El Monte.

Jimmy Nguyen – I am a current student with Pasadena City College. So, I would like to
address Mayor Jessica Ancona and Mayor Pro Tem Vicky Martinez in particular. There
was a recent article published with San Gabriel Valley Tribune describing how former
Chief of Police Ken Weldon made homophobic slurs to a former El Monte elected official.
I'm here to denounce this type of behavior by a man who I find very hard to believe, was
a former Chief of Police. This City Council, including the both of you have preached to us
about how bad anti-hate speech is and that content like this should not be permitted. Yet
you both associate with this man and allow him to sponsor your political fundraisers
defending him and taking funds from him. If this continues, you both are nothing more than
hypocrites with empty words. Please remember that no amount of money in the world
makes it acceptable for a person to use hateful speech towards any group of people, you
cannot buy friends and loyalty. You must condemn this man and his speech and to never
associate with him nor take any campaign funds from him again and actually you must
return every penny that this man has given to you. This man does not do anything for
free, has given to the community yes, but he has taken more than you think. You have
talked about corruption recently over something that might be a mistake of the mind, not
the heart on social media on your Twitter page Mayor, yet failed to mention your own
involvement with this corrupt man, which makes you implicated in any cases of corruption
unless you denounce him tonight. I do have to say, as a side note, but I love the farmers
markets, and we'll say that the Valley Mall is looking better. And I will commend City
Manager Alma Martinez for this and any other community programs and events that she
is responsible for. She has initiated many programs when the community was in need
during the pandemic and you both have put her down, did not attend these events, and
now demand credit for something, you have absolutely nothing to do with. It is a good try

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 1, 2021

on your part but please I'm begging you and my El Monte citizens that we need you to do
better.

Andre Quintero – I don’t know how many Council Communications you are going to get to
tonight but for things that are not on the agenda I just wanted the Council to consider you
know. We had a President that governed by tweet not very effective in my opinion and
competent. We have a chance you have a chance here to do some really special things
with the City, you’re on a good foundation financially with the COVID relief package that
was passed by the legislature, the federal legislature and signed by the President. You
are going to have resources now to be able to do a lot of important things that this
community needs. Unfortunately, if you continue to persist on an agenda of vindictiveness
and retaliation and not focus on the things that are most important for this community
you're gonna miss this golden opportunity that you have. So, I encourage all of you to
really focus on those things that matter most in our community, whether it's economic
development, developing the budget, our roads that need some serious help. I don’t know
if you have noticed, but we've also been seeing a lot of graffiti, and specifically the type of
graffiti that is very dangerous gang related graffiti. I know there is a wall very close to
where I live that's been tagged at least two or three times and every time I brought it to
the attention of staff, they've been diligent about getting it removed as they should. But it's
been throughout different parts of the community on the south side, on the north side, on
Lower Azusa and Cedar and you know it's even surprising, the folks that are in that
neighborhood, not reporting it or not getting it down sooner. I saw one big piece of graffiti
that was around for at least a day before it was removed. That is kind of the broken window
theory of crime, that we want to make sure that we address as quickly as possible.
Strongly encouraged as part of this budget to look at new police officers because frankly
you're going to be losing a number of police officers, over the next couple of years through
attrition. So, it's really important that you start preparing and it's a great opportunity right
now to have those types of hires when you do have the one-time funds that help you
replenish the force that we have. They've done an outstanding job over the last 11 years
bringing down crime precipitously in the last five years, it's been a little bit challenging with
Prop 37 and another initiatives that have changed the laws at the statewide level it has
been challenging to be able to address crime but it is possible work closely with the district
attorney's office to make sure that they address quality of life crimes, misdemeanor
offenses that a lot of times we don't even focus on because we're thinking of Part 1 crimes,
but these are crimes that will affect our community. So, I would encourage you to have
that relationship. You're going to hear a lot of things tonight from a lot of different folks. I
would just encourage you to remember to keep perspective, when you're out there, you're
going to hear a lot of different things. So just keep that perspective and that balance, best
wishes to all of you.

Miguel Aguayo – Some events in the life of corrupt Kenny Weldon, [inaudible] qualified,
former Police Chief of El Monte a major political supporter of Mayor Ancona and Mayor
Pro Tem Martinez Muela. Corrupt Kenny with a political [inaudible] from retired Chief
Wayne Clayton any physical adversary. Many individuals have driven around the City with
him during the middle of the night to steal lawn signs. He's also good at using [inaudible]
midgets to do his dirty work from him. This is how he was given the role of police chief, he
cashed in a career’s worth of political favors. Corrupt Kenny Weldon became chief of
police without a college degree. He never promoted to a single rank of sergeant, or
lieutenant, or captain or assistant chief. He received an appointment created by Wayne
Clayton for individuals too dumb or unqualified to pass a standard civil service examination
and promote legitimately. Kenny never obtained a college degree, and as a matter of fact

  7
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 1, 2021

the El Monte City Charter had to be changed to allow this inept man to become the chief
of police. The current Chief of Police David Reynoso has a bachelor's and master's
degree is a graduate of a prestigious FBI National Academy and honorably served our
country as member of the United States Marine Corps. Weldon cleaned up crimes for
former Mayor Ernie Gutierrez including a traffic collision under Mayor Gutierrez was drunk.
Don’t believe it ask retired police officers. Put them under oath and ask them of the dozens
of domestic situations that were swept under the rug as well. We should ask the last retired
EMPD dispatch manager why Weldon’s wife would call police dispatch crying. Anyone
who knows Weldon knows that he had a drinking problem, and an anger management
problem a scary set of traits. Weldon used the undercover detectives of the Police
Department to follow his wife around when he thought she was cheating on him. Don't
believe me, ask EMPD detectives. Ironic side note, Ken Weldon has disrespected his wife
and family for decades, with his very well-known mistress and infidelity. Someone should
ask why Weldon had a personal office on the top floor of the Chase building that was given
to him rent free for years. I wonder what he did in this office. Weldon used his position as
Chief to get his daughter a slap on the wrist for a possession of narcotics for sales arrest
while in possession of a loaded firearm. Unfortunately, her Latino boyfriend that was with
her at the time of her arrest got a prison sentence, abuse of authority, anyone. I won’t
have time for the rest but Mayor, Mayor Pro Tem and everybody do not compromise
yourself or your responsibility to the City by associating or accepting dirty money from this
man who was chief. You might say he gives to the community, but remember this man
has never done anything without asking you for something in return. It looks like you owe
to him, and he is demanding payment from you.

Eva Stoltz - I am been told that nothing can be done about all this sidewalk selling. I don't
believe that for a minute. Why don't you change code enforcement hours and have them
out there on the streets when the people are doing all their selling, especially on the
weekends. They are blocking sidewalks that people have to walk around in the street to
get by you can just ask Mr. Hoffman about that because it's happened to him. Do we have
to bring in the ADA since code enforcement, and the police can't or won't do anything to
make people comply with the rules. They are allowed one chair and no tables this is not
happening. They are required to display City issued permits, LA County Health permits
and business licenses. They are to display it on the street side portion of the vending
location at all times. So, all the rules are being broken, and it doesn't look like our City
cares. Also, I just read to they are not allowed in residential areas. I can show you three
places already that I've seen, while they're popping up and they're selling right in front of
their houses. At the last meeting all I heard was talk about meetings and committees not
one word about what is being done to better our City. Since El Monte is receiving all this
federal money do something to better our City. Try to bring investors, try to bring in a good
market. We don't need any more housing, low income or otherwise. It's always been said,
keep and spend your tax dollars in El Monte. Where the corner taco stands? And speaking
of tax dollars are these people paying taxes? Please don't take me for an idiot because
the honor system doesn’t work here. Also, the last meeting Mrs. Powers mentioned some
of the Council do not pay attention when people are speaking and I watched and what she
is saying is the truth and I think this is very rude. Also keeping us waiting for longer than
an hour to start the meeting at 7:00 o’clock is rude and inconsiderate. I was shocked that
the meeting started today at seven o'clock but we know why because of these
presentations and these people that were here. Our City is looking like a dump and no
one cares. We are becoming the laughing stock of the San Gabriel Valley and our Council
is leading the parade. Thank you for your attention to those matters.

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 1, 2021

Samuel Urias – I see there has been a great deal of effort trying to paint Chief Reynoso
as improperly influencing a security guard contract. If he was trying to improperly influence
a contract why would he report his employment on his Form 700. He has publicly reported
it in the past along with his role working in operations because you aren't aware operations
is not sales and marketing he had no ownership and is no longer employed by this
company he has offered to provide all financial documents to prove he benefited nothing
from the contract. Additionally, was the City's procurement procedure followed, yes. Were
other bids obtained and considered, yes. Was Chief Reynoso involved in the review or
discussion of the bids, no. Has the City Attorney explained to you that this is a confidential
personnel matter, yes. Did one of you violate the Brown Act and leak this to the press,
anyway, very likely. A Tribune article said the Police Department vetted this company
that is absolutely not true this was done by another City Department. Now I'd like to discuss
another recent contract since we were on the topic of transparency and conflict of interest.
On February 16th the Council was presented with a $8.0 to $10.0 million energy contract
by Alliance Building Solutions. In open session we heard Mayor Ancona state that the City
staff was approached by the vendor, since no RFP or request for competitive bids was
ever initiated by the City. Later Council person Morales asked questions about how this
vendor initiated its relationship with the City. In other words, where did this vendor come
from, who personally contacted this vendor and vouch for them, we then learned that the
initial meeting was composed of Mayor Ancona, the City Manager, and Alliance Building
Solutions reps including a consultant former State Assemblyman Roger Hernandez. So,
as we demand transparency for this $150,000 security contract which Chief Reynoso is
very open to and of which approximately 97% of the funds go to pay security guard
salaries. I think the Council should also direct an investigation into who initiated the first
Alliance Building Solutions meeting with the City staff, after all the meeting led to an $8.0
dollar plus contract being presented to Council with no RFP or other competitive bidding.
As a side note, the investigation should concurrently, focus on the nature of Mayor
Ancona’s relationship with Roger Hernandez talk about a conflict of interest. In closing this
attack on Chief Reynoso is a poor attempt to deflect the attention away from the hateful,
homophobic bigot who has Mayor Ancona and Mayor Pro Tem Martinez Muela in his
pocket. Chief Reynoso has exposed this man for what he is. Mayor Ancona and Mayor
Pro Tem Martinez Muela would advise you to prepare yourself to defend your
unconscionable acceptance of this man support, or find your moral compass and a
backbone and renounce him, he called one of your colleagues, I quote... If you ever meant
anything you have ever said about stopping hate return every penny Ken Weldon donated
to your election, even the money you raised at a recent golf tournament put on by former
Chief of Police Ken Weldon. We will be watching.

Gabriel Ramirez –So first, let me get this straight, so I know at the last City Council meeting
I wasn’t here but I was watching on closed session on how the previous regime was
speaking on the audits. It’s time for the City Council to really look at the audits because
for the past years with the regimes that we’ve had in the City Council are very scared.
What is it that you are hiding for? Why is it that we haven’t pushed the audits? You talk
about transparency. You talk about hypocrisy, well there it is. Look at the previous times
when they voted on and you want to question it. Currently, if I were you guys check the
tapes and see for yourself how many times I've been violated and also violations of
speakers like myself and those who couldn't speak. I remember the previous times
Councilmember at the time Jessica Ancona and Vicky Martinez Muela you’ve seen the
violations of the regime that have violated the Brown Act and questioning the member of
the public saying where did you get the law degree at. So, if you really want to talk about
that then, it's time for the City Council to really push the audits. Because ever since

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of June 1, 2021

Montebello, Lynwood, other cities, Baldwin Park have been already audited and is that we
are hiding for because there is a lot of things that should be exposed and I really hope that
this City Council really go for it, and really speak out for the truth.

Mike Gomez – I am Mike Gomez and I have been an El Monte resident for almost 40
years. Now I've been involved with the City for over 10 years serving on a number of
committees and commissions, including Art and Public Places, the 100th Anniversary
Committee, Public Access, the Measure GG Tax Oversight Committee, the Sister City
Cultural Commission, and as an Interim Planning Commissioner on the El Monte Planning
Commission. I currently serve as Vice Chair on the Measure EM Committee, and also
serve as the Los Angeles County Commissioner, having served as Chair of the Los
Angeles County Consumer Affairs Advisory Commission 2019 through 2020. Now the
reason that I highlight my civic involvement, over the years is because I see things that
are presently happening in our City, which are very concerning and I want to call your
attention to them. Now there have been a couple of articles in the past few weeks, which
have been critical of our Chief of Police David Reynoso. I want to state that I completely
support our Chief, and I believe that we're very fortunate to have him as our Chief of Police.
Crime in El Monte has been the lowest that it has been in years thanks to him and the fine
work of our El Monte Police Officers and our Chief has been able to do this with fewer
resources and fewer officers, then any other chief has had. Our City and community is
safer because of his leadership and in my opinion, he is the best Chief, that we have ever
had in our City. I would also like to commend the work and the incredible leadership of our
City Manager Alma Martinez. Alma Martinez has kept the City afloat during this once in a
lifetime health crisis of the COVID pandemic. She's also taken on the task of Public
